items.title: I Beat Jev AI with a Fine-Tuned Open-Source Model
items.summary: A fine-tuned open-source decision model beat Jev AI on my own production data. It has 436M parameters, trained in about 25 minutes, and runs locally. Decision models like Jev put fast, calibrated decisions where LLM latency can't reach. In this video I fine-tune GLiNER2.5-Decide into "Postie", a local model that decides which AI agent should wake for each new post in my agent workspace. We cover the use case, building the dataset with Sonnet 5.5, the training format, the model's architecture, and the results against Jev on accuracy, calibration, speed and cost. 📌 Read the article: https://www.jamesbriggs.io/beating-jev-with-oss 📌 See the base GLiNER model in 3D: https://spacesheep.dev/@james/jev-86-base-gliner-in-3d What we found: - Right agent: Local picks the right agent on 85.9% of 205 test posts, against Jev's 78.0%. With our rules added, the pipeline reaches 91.7%. - Calibration: Local's calibration error (ECE) on picking the agent is 0.052, against Jev's 0.071. - Speed: ~27 ms per decision on an RTX 5000 Ada laptop GPU and ~176 ms on an M4 Max, against ~328 ms for Jev over the network. On an M1 MacBook Air (CPU only) it is slower: ~1,457 ms. - Cost: under 0.1¢/1K decisions on the M4 Max, against Jev's 5¢/1K. - Data: 3,659 labelled posts from my own workspace, labelled by Sonnet 5.5 and rules. ⏱️ Chapters 0:00 Intro 1:45 Jev and calibrated decisions 5:03 The catch 7:04 A real use case: waking the right agent 12:55 The two decisions 13:42 Building the dataset 16:42 Splitting by date 18:12 Training rows and two calls 21:44 Inside GLiNER2.5-Decide 25:42 Results against Jev 27:02 Speed on each machine 29:09 Cost 30:16 What to make of local decision models 📚 Links Beating Jev with OSS (article): https://www.jamesbriggs.io/beating-jev-with-oss Understanding Jev (the previous video): https://youtu.be/P-t4F_UlxkI Understanding Jev (article): https://www.jamesbriggs.io/understanding-jev GLiNER2.5 (Fastino): https://fastino.ai/blog/gliner2-5-span-free-information-extraction GLiNER2 paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18546 On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks (2017): https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599 TypeSafe, Introducing System One Models & Jev: https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev Semantic Router: https://www.aurelio.ai/semantic-router 👋 Find me X: https://x.com/jamescalam LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamescalam/ GitHub: https://github.com/jamescalam #JevAI #GLiNER #FineTuning
